messages:
alex: CI on my feature branch `feature/asset-pipeline` is red on linux-shard-4 but passes locally. I rebased onto main yesterday — any quick ideas?
ci-bot: build failed in shard 4 (linux). Failing test: TestImageResizePipeline -> assertion error at image_processor.py:214
alex: here's the failing snippet from the CI log:
```
E       AssertionError: expected 256x256 got 0x0
File: /app/asset_pipeline/image_processor.py:214
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tests/test_image_pipeline.py", line 87, in test_resize_pipeline
    assert resized.size == (256, 256)
```
maya: did you run the same docker image locally? sometimes the CI base image changed. also: any changed deps in your branch?
sam: try a single-test run on CI or rerun shard first: `/rerun shard=4` — if it flakes we can bisect.
jin: TestImageResize has been flaky before when libjpeg version mismatch happens. check pip freeze or image libs (libjpeg-turbo). locally maybe you have system libs different from CI.
alex: i ran `pytest tests/test_image_pipeline.py::test_resize_pipeline` inside `docker://redwood/ci:linux-2025` and it passed. only CI shard failing. I did merge `main` yesterday which included a protobuf bump and a small image metadata change from @marco.
maya: protobuf bump could change serialization logic; but that shouldn't change image sizes. more likely an environment race (tmp dir) or a test ordering flake. can you paste the full test run from CI?
ci-bot: full failing job url: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/12345 (artifact: logs/shard-4.log)
alex: linking relevant commits from my branch after rebasing: abc1234..def5678 (I added change to asset ingestion ordering).
sam: if it's only on the shard, start with `/rerun job=12345 shard=4` to get a clean run. if it repros consistently, do `git bisect` between abc1234 and def5678 locally using the CI image. quick bisect commands:
```
git bisect start def5678 abc1234
# run failing test in bisect script inside docker image
# git bisect run ./ci/scripts/run_single_test.sh tests/test_image_pipeline.py::test_resize_pipeline
```
jin: alternatively try isolating the test: `pytest -k test_resize_pipeline -q --maxfail=1 -s` in CI image to see flakier output (timing print). Also check for usage of tmp directories in test that might collide.
alex: triggered rerun: `/rerun job=12345 shard=4` (requested)
oncall-bot: Rerun queued by alex — job 12345 shard 4. Expected start in ~30s.
maya: if rerun fails again, @sam can you help run a bisect? i might also try reproducing on an AWS instance with the same image.
sam: happy to. if bisect points to your last merge commit, we can revert or patch the failing logic. if it's a flaky infra thing, we'll file infra ticket.
ci-bot: rerun finished: same failure reproduced on shard 4.
alex: ack. starting bisect now, will post results here.
(30 minutes later)
alex: bisect found the culprit: commit `d4e9f1b` (merged from main) — it changed how we construct PIL Image from bytes, added a fallback that returns an empty image on decode failure. looks like the CI image lib exposes a new code path that returns empty size instead of raising.
jin: thanks — sounds like we should make the code robust (validate image.size) rather than hide decode errors. can you prepare a small patch that raises on invalid size?
alex: will open a PR with a short fix + unit asserting decode errors are explicit. tagging for review.
maya: +1, also add a short note in the test to avoid masking upstream lib changes.
sam: if you want a quick mitigation, we can add a temporary test skip on linux-shard-4 only, but better to fix.
alex: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/asset-pipeline/pull/782 — includes fix + changelog. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
